sentence: This project uses many kinds of molecular data to find genetic variants, reactive antigens and disease mechanisms behind an autoimmune blistering skin disease called pemphigus.
This project studies how 3D genome folding controls gene expression, using methods that reach very high resolution.
This project studies how complex genetic variations linked to neurodevelopmental diseases affect neuronal activity in human patient populations.
This project tries to find out what a marker of endometrial stem cells does in endometriosis inflammation, using mouse models and organoids.
This project studies which types of T cells take part in tendon healing and tests the role of a signaling protein.
This project studies how microsporidia parasites grow inside their host cells, using cellular, proteomic and structural approaches to examine the space where they replicate.
This project builds math tools with drag-and-drop, audio and physical-piece interfaces using computer vision, for people who are blind or have low vision.
This project develops better and cheaper methods of detecting somatic mutations that are likely to influence human biology.
This project develops a system that uses known donor and patient information at the time of an organ offer to match donor lungs with patients.
This project acquires a confocal microscope to support studies of neurodegenerative diseases, the effects of forever chemicals, and brain health and behavior.
This project tries to find out how HIV enters its natural host T cells and starts an infection.
This project builds a hydrogel that slowly releases nerve growth factor to the cornea and tests it in models of diabetic keratopathy.
This project tries to find out how a transcription recycling mechanism drives lethal prostate cancer and develops an RNA targeting nanotherapy against it.
This project studies how ethanol changes the strength and plasticity of excitatory glutamatergic inputs to the prefrontal cortex in female and male mice.
This project builds rat models of hormone-dependent male breast cancer to learn how hormones affect the disease and its response to therapy.
This project studies how a lung protein called follistatin-like protein 1 helps the host defend against bacterial pneumonia.
This project uses cellular models of synaptic pruning to study how risk genes for schizophrenia act in human microglia and neurons.
This project tests a mobile app that uses wearable sensor technology and real-time behavioral support to help people with HIV quit smoking.
This project uses electrophysiological, behavioral and cell type-specific techniques in mice to study how neurotensin affects methamphetamine self-administration and relapse.
This project studies how a protein controls totipotency, zygotic genome activation and early embryonic development in mice.
